subject: Architecture
title: Great Zimbabwe: Stone City of Southern Africa
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Great Zimbabwe: Stone City of Southern Africa.

hook.text: Colonial Europeans refused to believe Africans built Great Zimbabwe. They were wrong.

buildup.text: Great Zimbabwe's walls rise 36 feet high and are 16 feet thick — built without mortar from granite blocks.

discovery.text: The Great Enclosure's outer wall curves for 820 feet — the largest ancient structure in sub-Saharan Africa.

twist.text: Cecil Rhodes and other colonialists attributed it to Phoenicians or Arabs. Archaeology proved it was Shona.

climax.text: At its peak, Great Zimbabwe was a trading hub connecting gold mines to Indian Ocean ports.

punchline.text: They denied African genius for a century. The stones told a different story.

quiz.question: Who built Great Zimbabwe according to archaeological evidence?
options: The Shona people of southern Africa
Arab merchants from the Indian Ocean

details.summary: Great Zimbabwe was a medieval stone city in southern Africa built between the 11th and 15th centuries without mortar, using precisely fitted granite blocks. Its Great Enclosure wall stands 11 meters tall and 5 meters thick, making it the largest ancient stone structure in sub-Saharan Africa.
details.whyItMatters: Great Zimbabwe disproves colonial-era claims that sub-Saharan Africans couldn't build monumental architecture. It was the center of a wealthy trading civilization connected to Indian Ocean commerce spanning from China to Arabia.
takeaways: Built between the 11th and 15th centuries without mortar
The Great Enclosure wall stands 11 meters tall and 5 meters thick
It was sub-Saharan Africa's largest ancient stone structure

faq.question: Who built Great Zimbabwe?
faq.answer: The ancestors of the modern Shona people built Great Zimbabwe as the center of a wealthy cattle and gold-trading civilization. Colonial-era Europeans falsely attributed it to Phoenicians or other outsiders, but archaeological evidence conclusively proves local African construction.

faq.question: What was traded at Great Zimbabwe?
faq.answer: Gold, ivory, and cattle from the interior were exchanged for glass beads, porcelain from China, and cloth from the Swahili coast and beyond. Artifacts from as far as China and Persia demonstrate extensive participation in Indian Ocean trade networks.
